title: Sheaf-algebra extensions and the first two cotangent Ext groups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\mathcal G$ be any $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with no quasi-coherence assumption. On $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ let $\mathscr E_f(\mathcal G)$ be the groupoid of extensions $0\to\mathcal G\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal A\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal O_X\to0$ of sheaves of commutative $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-algebras, with kernel an ideal of square zero inducing the given $\mathcal O_X$-action on $\mathcal G$; morphisms induce the identity on the kernel and quotient. For $\mathrm{NL}$ and derived Ext as in [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex], there is a canonical bijection $\pi_0\mathscr E_f(\mathcal G)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathrm{NL}_{X/B},\mathcal G)$ taking $\mathcal O_X\oplus\mathcal G$ to zero. It is natural under every $\mathcal O_X$-linear coefficient map $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$: pushout of an extension induces $u_*$ on Ext. The Baer sum, formed by the fibre product of two extensions over $\mathcal O_X$ followed by pushout of $\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal G$ along addition, corresponds to addition in Ext. For each such extension its automorphisms inducing the identity on kernel and quotient are canonically the additive group $\operatorname{Ext}^0_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathrm{NL}_{X/B},\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\Omega_{X/B},\mathcal G)$. Here $\Omega_{X/B}=H^0(\mathrm{NL}_{X/B})$; the isomorphism sends $d:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G$, an $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-derivation, to $a\mapsto a+i(d(p(a)))$. Composition corresponds to addition of derivations, and this automorphism identification is natural under coefficient pushout.

source.place: Tags 0GQ5 (lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi), 0GQ6 (remark-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi), 0GQ7 (lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi-functorial), 0GQ8 (remark-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi-functorial), and 08UG (lemma-huge-diagram-ringed-topoi), clause (2), with identity underlying topos. The Baer-sum clause is not stated in Stacks: it follows from the explicit description of the class in 0GQ6 (choose one sheaf of sets E mapping to both extensions; the class of the fibre-product-then-sum extension is the sum of the two induced maps J/J^2 -> G), together with the torsor of 08UK (lemma-choices-ringed-topoi).

proof.text: Put $A=f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$ and $O=\mathcal O_X$. The definition identifies $\mathrm{NL}_{X/B}$ with $\mathrm{NL}_{O/A}$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. For any sheaf polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow O$ use $J,M=J/J^2,F,K=[M\to F]$ and $\lambda_E$ from the comparison node. The two-term boundary node gives $\partial_E:\operatorname{Hom}_O(M,\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_O(K,\mathcal G)$, with kernel the maps $\theta d_E$. The cokernel comparison and that node give $\operatorname{Ext}^0_O(\mathrm{NL}_{O/A},\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Hom}_O(\Omega_{O/A},\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Der}_A(O,\mathcal G)$. All results apply to arbitrary module sheaves, so no quasi-coherence or finiteness hypothesis is introduced.

Given an extension $\mathcal T\twoheadrightarrow O$, take $E$ to be its underlying sheaf of sets, mapped to $O$. The polynomial universal property on each $A(U)[E(U)]$, followed by the universal property of the sheafification $P=A[E]$ (as $\mathcal T$ is a sheaf of $A$-algebras), gives the $A$-algebra map $a:P\to\mathcal T$ with $[e]\mapsto e$. Its restriction to $J$ has values in $\mathcal G$ and annihilates $J^2$, because the kernel is square zero. Thus it defines an $O$-linear map $\delta_a:M\to\mathcal G$. Define $c(\mathcal T)=\partial_E(\delta_a)\lambda_E^{-1}$. More generally one can use any such $E$ with a lift $E\to\mathcal T$. Two choices have a common presentation using $E\amalg E'$, whose lift is their combined lift. Under the canonical presentation comparisons, the two restrictions of its conormal map give the same derived class, by naturality of the boundary. Hence $c$ is independent of the choices. An isomorphism of extensions preserves its conormal map after composing the lift, so $c$ is defined on isomorphism classes.

For injectivity, take two extensions $\mathcal T_1,\mathcal T_2$ with equal classes and use $E=\mathcal T_1\times_O\mathcal T_2$. Both projections are surjective as sheaf maps; write $a:P\to\mathcal T_1$, $b:P\to\mathcal T_2$ and $\delta_1,\delta_2:M\to\mathcal G$. Equality of classes and boundary exactness give $\delta_2-\delta_1=\theta d_E$ for some $\theta:F\to\mathcal G$. Set $D=\theta\circ(\mathrm d\otimes1):P\to\mathcal G$ and $b'=b-i_2D$. Leibniz and the square-zero kernel show $b'(xy)=b'(x)b'(y)$; $b'$ is additive and fixes $A$. For $j\in J$, $b'(j)=i_2\delta_1(\bar j)$. Thus $b'$ annihilates $\ker a$, while $a$ is locally surjective because $E\to\mathcal T_1$ is. It descends uniquely to $h:\mathcal T_1\to\mathcal T_2$, inducing identity on $O$ and $\mathcal G$. Locally, $h(t)=0$ forces $p_1(t)=0$ and then $t=i_1g$ with $g=0$; given $t_2$, lift its quotient locally to $t_1$ and correct $t_2-h(t_1)$ in the kernel. Hence $h$ is an isomorphism of sheaves and of extensions.

source.place: Tag 08UG proof Steps 1-3, specialized to identity underlying topos and unchanged base

proof.text: For surjectivity take $\xi$ and its representative $\delta:J/J^2\to\mathcal G$ supplied by the representative node. Form the square-zero semidirect ring sheaf $Q\ltimes\mathcal G$, where $Q=P/J^2$ acts on $\mathcal G$ through $O$ and $(q,g)(q',g')=(qq',\bar qg'+\bar q'g)$. Quotient by the image of $J/J^2\to Q\ltimes\mathcal G$, $m\mapsto(m,-\delta(m))$. This image is an ideal: multiplication by $(q,g)$ gives $(qm,-\bar q\delta(m))=(qm,-\delta(qm))$. Call the quotient $\mathcal T_\delta$. The map $g\mapsto[(0,g)]$ is injective because an element $(0,g)$ in that graph has $m=0$ and hence $g=0$. The quotient map to $O$ is locally surjective, and any local kernel class $[(m,g)]$ equals $[(0,g+\delta(m))]$. These statements remain true after taking sheaf quotients, by local representatives. Thus $\mathcal T_\delta$ is an extension with square-zero kernel $\mathcal G$. Its lift $P\to\mathcal T_\delta$, $p\mapsto[(p,0)]$, sends $j$ to $i(\delta(\bar j))$. Its class is therefore exactly $\xi$. This proves the canonical bijection, not just an abstract torsor assertion.

source.place: Tags 08UJ and 08UK, pushout construction; direct verification of the omitted quotient calculation

proof.text: For the split extension $O\oplus\mathcal G$, use $E=O$ and the lift $x\mapsto(x,0)$. Its polynomial map kills $J$, so its conormal map is zero and its class is zero. This also fixes the origin of the canonical bijection.

source.place: Tag 0GQ5 proof, split origin, and Tag 0GQ6

proof.text: For $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$, the coefficient pushout of $\mathcal T$ is $(\mathcal T\ltimes\mathcal H)/\{(i(g),-u(g))\}$, where $\mathcal T$ acts through $O$. The graph is an ideal by $O$-linearity of $u$; the same local kernel calculation as in Step 4 gives an extension by $\mathcal H$. A lift $P\to\mathcal T$ followed by the canonical map to this quotient has conormal map $u\delta$. By postcomposition naturality of $\partial_E$, its class is $u_*c(\mathcal T)$. This proves naturality even when $u$ is neither injective nor surjective; no flatness of $u$ is used.

For $\mathcal T_1,\mathcal T_2$ choose the common generator sheaf $E=\mathcal T_1\times_O\mathcal T_2$. The map $P\to\mathcal T_1\times_O\mathcal T_2$ restricts on $J/J^2$ to $(\delta_1,\delta_2)$ with values in $\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal G$. Pushing out by addition gives conormal map $\delta_1+\delta_2$. Since $\partial_E$ is additive, its class is $\partial_E(\delta_1+\delta_2)\lambda_E^{-1}=c(\mathcal T_1)+c(\mathcal T_2)$. This is precisely the stipulated fibre-product-then-addition Baer sum.

source.place: Tag 0GQ6 explicit representative, applied to the Baer construction; addition calculation by Q55

proof.text: For an $A$-derivation $d:O\to\mathcal G$ set $T_d(t)=t+i(d(p(t)))$. It fixes kernel and quotient. Expanding a product, the extra cross terms are $i(p(t)d(p(t'))+p(t')d(p(t)))=i(d(p(tt')))$ and the product of two kernel terms is zero. Hence $T_d$ is an $A$-algebra map, with inverse $T_{-d}$. Conversely, for an automorphism $T$ fixing the ends, $T-\mathrm{id}$ has values in $i(\mathcal G)$ and vanishes on the kernel. Local lifts through $p$ therefore define a unique additive sheaf map $d:O\to\mathcal G$, independent of lifts; multiplicativity of $T$ gives the displayed Leibniz rule, and fixing $A$ makes $d$ vanish on $A$. Thus every such $T$ is uniquely $T_d$. One has $T_dT_e=T_{d+e}$ since $pT_e=p$. With Step 1 this gives the stated additive automorphism identification with $\operatorname{Ext}^0$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\Omega_{X/B},\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Tag 08UG(2), specialized to an extension and itself; explicit derivation formula

proof.text: Let $q:\mathcal T\to u_*\mathcal T$ be coefficient pushout. Its kernel inclusion $i_{\mathcal H}$ satisfies $qi_{\mathcal G}=i_{\mathcal H}u$. Consequently $qT_d(t)=q(t)+i_{\mathcal H}(u(d(p(t))))=T_{ud}q(t)$. The induced automorphism fixes the added $\mathcal H$ summand in the explicit quotient of Step 6, so this equality identifies it on all local representatives. The universal-derivation identification and the degree-zero derived Hom isomorphism are natural in coefficients by the cited nodes. Thus automorphism pushout is exactly postcomposition by $u$ on both Hom and Ext, as required.

source.place: Tag 08UG(2); coefficient compatibility verified from the explicit pushout
